## 1. N6 call in the audit vs the P0.9 node whitelist

Spec: SPEC §10 + spec-factors §20.9; `test_lanes.py::test_audit_records_the_n6_call_and_its_gate_status` requires an
`llm_calls` entry with node `profile_consistency` in every Flow C audit, built from the `bedrock.call_tool` call of
`check_profile`.

Failing tests (they spy `bedrock.call_tool` and whitelist the nodes):
- `tests/test_pipeline_offline.py::test_review_nvda_llm_calls_are_explainer_only_for_the_three_failing_sections`
  (`nodes <= ALLOWED_NODES = {explainer, values_parser}`, line 369)
- `tests/test_pipeline_offline.py::test_review_nvda_audit_record`
  (audit `llm_calls` node list must equal the spy node list in order, line 403: the N6 call comes in the middle of the
  writer calls, because it runs as the "sixth lane" next to them; the audit lists writer calls in display order)
- `tests/test_pipeline_offline.py::test_review_current_portfolio_is_coherent_with_h6_h10_unknown` (`nodes <= {"explainer"}`, line 470)
- `tests/test_pipeline_offline.py::test_demo_reviews_the_personas_with_complete_fixtures_and_notices_the_rest`
  (`<= ALLOWED_NODES`, line 570)

The whitelist predates D8 (it encodes D7 "no N1/N2/N4", written before N6 existed). It must allow `profile_consistency`
(and the audit/spy order check must tolerate the N6 call).

## 2. Call-for-call order vs parallel lanes

Spec: spec-factors §20.10 / D8.2 (non-pass sections narrated concurrently on a ThreadPoolExecutor, max_workers=5).

- `tests/test_explain.py::test_same_inputs_same_explanation` asserts `llm.calls == first_calls` ("call for call"): the
  order of `bedrock.call_tool` calls across sections of two runs. With concurrent lanes the order of calls from different
  sections is scheduling-dependent (it fails on every run here). The explanation itself (`second == first`) is identical;
  only the interleaving of spy records differs. Keeping a fixed global call order would mean serialising the LLM calls,
  which defeats §20.10.

Needed from a human: update the five tests above (allow `profile_consistency` in the node whitelists; compare the
writer calls per section / as a sorted multiset instead of the global order) or tell me which one to give up.
